To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
kNN, L1S and WORD are the best methods for text categorization, and that Naive Bayes is not.

kNN is the most robust method, that LLSF and the neural network method are the best performers, that the performance of the learning algorithms is comparable, and that the inclusion of unlabelled data has a significant negative impact on the observed performance.

1) kNN, LLLSF and WORD performed best on the Reuters corpus, and the differences in the performance among these three classifiers were not statistically significant; 2) the performance of the other learning algorithms were also relatively good; 3) the performance of a Naive Baye's method was not as good as that of the other learning methods; 4) the performance of classifiers on some versions of the Reuters corpus was affected significantly by the inclusion of the unlabelled data
In summary, our research is concerned with
two aspects of text categorization: (1) a comparative evaluation of text categorization algorithms; and (2) a controlled study of the impact of configuration variation on the observed performance.
a comparative evaluation of text categorization techniques, and the results are useful for understanding the strengths and weaknesses of various methods and their potential applications.
the evaluation of a variety of text categorization techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of a classifier depends on the nature of the corpus used for training and evaluation.
the performance of a classifier on the Reuters corpus is highly dependent on the version of the corpus used in the experiment.
the performance of text categorization is very much dependent upon the corpus, classifier, and configuration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no single classifier that is the best for all text categorization tasks.

the performance of a text categorization system is highly dependent on the choice of the training set, the representation scheme and the learning algorithm, and that a good performance can be obtained using a wide-range of approaches.
the choice of a text classifier depends on many factors, including the application, the nature of the data, the available resources, the time constraint, and so forth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a text categorization method is highly sensitive to the choice of a training corpus.
the choice of the classifier and the configuration parameters are more important than the choice of the statistical features for text categorization.
a careful design of experiments and the use of a wide-range and diverse set of text categorization algorithms is necessary to provide a comprehensive evaluation of text categorization.
